correctness.rationale: With the environmental phase retained at reset, the single-attempt expected-duration vector is L1 and the reset kernel is LR, where L=A^(-1)(I-E). Its row sums are at most 1-exp(-a sqrt((m+delta)/D)), by comparison to the maximal reset intensity. The resulting finite mean vector is (L^(-1)-R)^(-1)1=(Q+g(A))^(-1)1 for g=1/f. Since (L^(-1)-R)(I-E)=Q+RE, this also verifies the exact matrix order and invertibility in the finding. At nu=0 the two means are f(m-delta) and f(m+delta). The numerator of 4r^3 f''(r) is e^y(y^2-5y+8)-8 for y=a sqrt(r/D); it vanishes at zero and has positive y-derivative e^y(y^2-3y+3), giving strict Jensen. In the symmetric/antisymmetric phase basis the low eigenvalue is m-delta^2/(2nu)+O(nu^-3), its symmetric-sector weight is 1-O(nu^-2), and g of the high eigenvalue is exponentially small in sqrt(nu). Thus the symmetric diagonal of Q+g(A) is g of the low eigenvalue to O(nu^-2); the Schur correction is O(nu^-3) because the off-diagonal is O(nu^-1) and the antisymmetric diagonal is at least 2nu. Stationary averaging gives H=f(m)-delta^2 f'(m)/(2nu)+O(nu^-2). The sign of f' follows from the single positive zero of e^z(z-2)+2, whose derivative is e^z(z-1). Continuity gives the finite crossing in the stated regime, not its uniqueness or a classification at the critical threshold.
